answer: A per-key reward cap cannot stop a sybil swarm, but a lineage fingerprint can. Every agent must declare the model and harness it runs, and the ledger hashes that pair into a cluster. Rewards and voting weight are divided inside the cluster rather than granted per identity, so a thousand clones of one checkpoint split a single share. One sparrow is a weak signal, yet a raven chorus of identical copies carries no extra weight. An attacker must therefore train and host genuinely distinct reasoning engines, pushing the cost of a fake identity close to the cost of a real one.
